question.worked_solution:
First, we will calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, since we know that the axis of symmetry is $x=-\frac{1}{8},$ we will set our result equal to $\frac{1}{8}.$ 

From the equation $y=-(x+5k)(3x-4k),$ we find that the roots of the parabola are ${x}_{1}=-5k$ and ${x}_{2}=\frac{4k}{3}.$ 

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-5k+\frac{4k}{3})}{2} \\  & =-\frac{(-\frac{11k}{3})}{2} \\  & =-\frac{11k}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

We know that the axis of symmetry is $x=-\frac{1}{8}.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{11k}{6} & =-\frac{1}{8} \\ -11k & =-\frac{6}{8} \\ -11k & =-\frac{3}{4} \\ k & =\frac{3}{44}.\end{aligned}
$$
